selector.description: Fail-closed scope routing and canonical-command validation.

rules.description: Pure core, lattice, and AI rules.

trajectory_contracts.description: Pure trajectory/volume/creation rules and their direct non-UI AI, command, and casting consumers.

contracts.description: Focused gameplay ECS contracts plus the renderer-free spell-resolution composition seam.

simulation.description: Deterministic multi-turn combat and CombatSummary snapshots.

app.description: Headless Campaign, Sandbox, Creator, gameplay application, and UI behavior.

map_unit.description: Map storage, settings, grid, and renderer-free publication units.

map_generation.description: Deterministic V1, V2, and V3 generation contracts and PR corpora.

map_contracts.description: Headless map publication, edit, presentation, and lifecycle contracts.

residual.description: All remaining non-map workspace and cross-owner contract tests.
command: not (package(hex_core) | package(hex_lattice) | package(hex_ai) | package(hex_units) | package(hex_combat_core) | package(hex_combat) | package(hex_test_support) | package(hex_gameplay_model) | package(hex_ui) | package(hex_map) | (package(hex_game) & binary(gameplay_app)))

rules.name: scope-routing-contract
rules.reason: Selector regression changes run their own fail-closed unit target; command manifests, selector engines, and CI topology remain fully fail-closed.

rules.name: scope-infrastructure
rules.reason: Validation infrastructure changes require the complete gate.

rules.name: map-contract-tests
rules.reason: Map integration tests exercise the explicit headless publication target.

rules.name: shared-test-app
rules.reason: The neutral app harness is validation infrastructure shared across owner partitions.

rules.name: map-generation
rules.reason: Map generation changes require their deterministic corpus and published-world contracts.

rules.name: map-publication
rules.reason: Map publication and presentation changes require unit and headless contract evidence.

rules.name: map-world-snapshot
rules.reason: The complete world snapshot adapter crosses generation, publication, multiplayer protocol, reconnect, and disclosure seams.

rules.name: map-foundations
rules.reason: Shared map foundations feed unit, generation, and publication contracts.

rules.name: terrain-impact-contract
rules.reason: The current shared file also owns the damaged-voxel projection consumed by map and application code; keep it fail-closed until those authorities are split by file.

rules.name: multiplayer-protocol
rules.reason: Shared wire, authorization, lobby, replica, and transport registration contracts require headless composition, residual protocol tests, strict docs/lints, and shipping compatibility without selecting map corpora.

rules.name: shared-core
rules.reason: Shared gameplay/world vocabulary has a workspace-wide consumer closure.

rules.name: world-owned
rules.reason: World-owned changes retain their existing complete owner and seam coverage.

rules.name: lattice-rules
rules.reason: Lattice rules flow through unit state and combat application.

rules.name: ai-rules
rules.reason: AI policy owns pure rules and feeds unit, combat, application, and shipping behavior.

rules.name: animation
rules.reason: Animation owns residual inline tests and crosses unit movement, combat lifecycle, and presentation.

rules.name: unit-trajectory-contracts
rules.reason: Trajectory and volume geometry use their pure rules plus direct creation, AI, command, and casting consumers; application/UI partitions cannot add authority evidence.

rules.name: units
rules.reason: Unit movement and state feed combat contracts and deployment/application seams.

rules.name: gameplay-screen-model
rules.reason: Pure gameplay screen models are consumed by headless UI behavior and the shipping application.

rules.name: runtime-ui
rules.reason: Presentation-only UI changes use pure view tests, the one headless app target, and shipping compilation without selecting map corpora.

rules.name: gameplay-visual
rules.reason: Gameplay-owned visual scripts prove presentation only; behavior remains in typed app and simulation oracles.

rules.name: combat-authority
rules.reason: Pure combat authority feeds ECS, summaries, application behavior, and shipping gameplay.

rules.name: combat
rules.reason: Combat adapters feed application summaries and gameplay projections.

rules.name: test-support
rules.reason: Shared test support is consumed by gameplay contracts, headless application tests, and map publication contracts.

rules.name: gameplay-assets
rules.reason: Gameplay schema and content own asset tests and flow into contracts, launches, and UI.

rules.name: shared-assets
rules.reason: Unclassified asset-loader, shared schema, or content changes cross ownership.

rules.name: gameplay-app-model
rules.reason: Gameplay-owned screen behavior needs model/app and shipping evidence.

rules.name: shared-app
rules.reason: Unclassified application composition may affect shared scenario or owner seams.

rules.name: developer-build-tooling
rules.reason: Developer build tooling requires lint and documentation validation.

rules.name: contributor-instructions
rules.reason: Contributor instructions need documentation and relative-link validation.

rules.name: documentation
rules.reason: Tracked Markdown needs documentation and relative-link validation.
